req.title: Init-db closes existing connection
req.statement: The system shall close any open connection before recreating the schema during init-db.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-042 requires that init-db closes any open connection before recreating the schema. The key behaviors to test are: (1) positive - init-db runs successfully and the DB is accessible afterward via HTTP (blog index returns 200); (2) negative - after init-db, a previously open connection is no longer the active one (close_db pops 'db' from g, so a new get_db() call returns a fresh connection); (3) boundary - calling init-db twice in sequence (the second call must also close the prior connection and succeed, not leave a dangling connection). We test via the Flask test client and the CLI runner, asserting exact status codes and exact output strings to maximize mutation kill rate. We also directly invoke close_db and get_db within an app context to verify the connection lifecycle.

tests.name: test_init_db_positive_blog_index_accessible
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp database path
init_db() called within an app context to bootstrap schema
actions: Create app with temp DB
Push app context and call init_db()
Pop app context (triggers close_db via teardown)
Use test client to GET / (blog index)
expected: Response body contains b'Flaskr' or is non-empty HTML
trace: R-FLASKR-042: init-db closes existing connection before recreating schema
After init-db completes, the app must serve requests normally
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db, close_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)

app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert len(r.data) > 0
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_init_db_negative_close_db_removes_connection_from_g
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp database path
An open DB connection exists in g before close_db is called
actions: Create app with temp DB
Push app context and call init_db() to open a connection
Call get_db() to confirm connection is in g
Call close_db() explicitly
Assert that g no longer holds 'db' key
expected: After close_db(), g.pop('db', None) returns None (connection was removed)
A subsequent get_db() call opens a fresh connection (not the closed one)
trace: R-FLASKR-042: close_db must pop 'db' from g and call .close() on it
If close_db does not remove the connection, g still holds the old one
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db, close_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)

app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    init_db()
    conn1 = get_db()
    assert 'db' in g
    close_db()
    assert g.pop('db', None) is None
    conn2 = get_db()
    assert conn2 is not conn1
    close_db()

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_init_db_cli_runner_outputs_initialized_message
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp database path
CLI command init-db registered via init_app
actions: Create app with temp DB
Invoke 'init-db' via Flask CLI test runner
Capture exit code and output
trace: R-FLASKR-042: init-db CLI command must complete successfully (exit 0) and emit the expected message
STC: state transition from uninitialized -> initialized via CLI trigger
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from click.testing import CliRunner
from flaskr.db import init_db_command

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)

app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    runner = CliRunner()
    result = runner.invoke(init_db_command)
    assert result.exit_code == 0
    assert 'Initialized the database.' in result.output

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_init_db_close_db_noop_when_no_connection
preconditions: No DB connection has been opened (g does not contain 'db')
actions: Create app with temp DB
Push app context without calling get_db()
Call close_db() directly
Assert no exception is raised and g still has no 'db' key
expected: close_db() returns without raising any exception
g.pop('db', None) returns None (nothing was there to close)
trace: R-FLASKR-042: close_db must be safe to call even when no connection is open
NEG: negative path - close_db with no prior connection must not crash
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flask import g
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import close_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)

app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    assert g.get('db') is None
    try:
        close_db()
        raised = False
    except Exception:
        raised = True
    assert raised == False
    assert g.pop('db', None) is None

os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_init_db_teardown_closes_connection_after_request
preconditions: Flask app created with TESTING=True and a temp database path
A request is made that opens a DB connection
actions: Create app with temp DB and call init_db()
Make a GET / request via test client (opens DB connection in g)
Make a second GET / request immediately after
Assert both responses return HTTP 200 (teardown closed prior connection cleanly)
expected: No exception raised between requests (teardown closed connection properly)
trace: R-FLASKR-042: teardown_appcontext(close_db) must close the connection after each request
STC: state transitions request1-open -> request1-close -> request2-open -> request2-close

from flaskr.db import init_db

with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r1 = client.get('/')
assert r1.status_code == 200

r2 = client.get('/')
assert r2.status_code == 200

os.unlink(path)
